A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PAFlow, and their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison. Added material and relocated appendix sections can be reliably distinguished.

before.justification: V1 reports original PAFlow experiments on CrossDocked2020 and Binding MOAD, together with component ablations, sensitivity studies, and atom-count analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds atom-count validation, molecular-structure evaluations, further baseline comparisons, and failure examples.

M1.justification: The coordinate VP flow, categorical atom-type formulation, interaction guidance, and noisy atom-number predictor remain unchanged. The training objectives and algorithms in Appendices B-C are retained; the comma correction in Equation 8 does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same molecular-generation task using CrossDocked2020 and Binding MOAD. The latter already appears in v1 Appendix E.1. V2's additional diagnostics and three selected test pockets do not introduce a new dataset, population, or task scenario.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets remain intact. V2 adds targeted appendix comparisons involving FLAG in Table 8, KGDiff in Table 10, and FlexSBDD in Table 11. FLAG and KGDiff were not included in v1's reported comparison tables.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation with atom-count intervals from 1,000 samples per selected protein, bond-length/angle/torsion distribution divergences, ring-size distributions, and PoseCheck strain-energy and clash measurements. These are protocols for added analyses; the original splits, training settings, and benchmark evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.6 tests how predicted atom counts align with reference ligands. E.7 adds extensive local and global structural-validity analyses, while F.4 presents explicit molecular failure cases. F.2 adds training-set affinity context. These substantially broaden validation beyond the retained component and sensitivity ablations.

E5.justification: Table 10 introduces 25th and 75th percentiles alongside median strain energy, adding distributional-spread reporting. These describe variation across molecules, not repeated-run uncertainty. Existing correlation tests remain unchanged; no seed counts, confidence intervals, or run-level error bars are added, and the new checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of error bars.

E6.justification: Tables 7-11 add atom-count, structural-quality, and comparator results, including PAFlow median strain energy of 90,239 and FlexSBDD average Vina Score of -6.64. F.2 newly reports training-set Vina mean/median of -8.19/-8.32. Figure 3 replaces the 3DZH example: Vina/QED/SA change from -10.25/0.52/0.57 to -10.64/0.59/0.63. This is a replacement example; the original Tables 1-6, including PAFlow's -8.31 headline score, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The proposition, mathematical formulations, and Appendix A proofs of equivariance, atom-type flow, guidance, and noise injection are retained. Minor notation and cross-reference edits introduce no new assumptions, derivations, or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scope: flow-based generation, prior interaction guidance, learned atom counts, and state-of-the-art reported binding affinity while maintaining favorable molecular properties. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations attributing affinity gains to reference-aligned atom counts and learned training-set binding patterns, discusses structural plausibility, and identifies improper double bonds, large rings, and fused rings as failures. The original pocket-estimation, rigid-protein, and single-objective limitations are retained under F.3.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and states that reproduction code is provided. It identifies PoseCheck for structural measurements and explicitly describes Vina-score labels for the interaction predictor. Appendix D's architecture, hyperparameters, and hardware information remain unchanged; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to CBGBench, PoseCheck, and FlexSBDD. Appendix F.1 extends the existing discussion of probability-path choices with a focused comparison to FlexSBDD, including flexible versus rigid protein modeling. The original related-work sections and principal research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. V2 adds acknowledgements, a NeurIPS checklist, and appendix discussion subsections, placing the former F and G material under F.3-F.4. Author affiliations and publication text change. References in Section 5.3 and Appendix A.4 now incorrectly point to Table 7 instead of Table 4.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual evidence with Tables 7-11 and a failure-example Figure 10, and replaces the 3DZH PAFlow panel in Figure 3. Table 11 redisplays several existing benchmark rows alongside FlexSBDD. The original appendix example figure is retained as Figure 11; existing ablation plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the paper more informative through structural-validity checks, atom-count validation, explicit failure examples, a FlexSBDD comparison, and a code-access pointer. However, its favorable structural interpretation underplays mixed evidence: Table 10 reports median strain energy of 90,239 for PAFlow versus 1,233 for TargetDiff. The added scrutiny improves transparency, but incomplete reconciliation of these results with the claims limits the overall gain.
